doc: Each case is built in a fresh temp root (unresolved temp path; on macOS the temp dir is itself a symlink that resolves elsewhere). Fields: modelDir (rel, created), extraDirs (rel, created), symlinks [{link,target}] (both rel to root, created after dirs), receipt (null | {text} | {base64}) written to <receiptBase or modelDir>.pull-receipt.json, inputPath (rel string appended verbatim to root; default modelDir) passed to derive. Placeholders in receipt text: {DIR}=root/modelDir unresolved, {DIR_RESOLVED}=its realpath, {OTHER}=an existing different dir, {ROOT}=root. expect: null | {repo,revision} | {conflict:{receiptRepo,pathRepo}}. knownPythonDivergence {pythonExpect,reason}, when present, is a documented Python-only difference (in the conservative direction) that the Python test pins instead of expect. Expectations are hand-authored from the documented rule except cases whose why says engine-observed. Checked by spike/Tests/HarnessCoreTests/PackIdentityConformanceTests.swift and scripts/tests/test_pack_identity_conformance.py.

cases.why: No receipt and no hub layout: no identity.
Valid receipt with dest naming the directory: repo and revision from the receipt.
dest resolves to a different existing directory: stale receipt reads as no receipt.
dest names a path that does not exist and is not the pack: no receipt.
dest is an empty string (not the pack): treated as a mismatching string dest, no receipt.
A stale receipt (dest elsewhere) naming another repo must not conflict with the hub path; the path identity applies.
A receipt with no dest key is trusted (sibling naming ties it to the path).
dest: null is not a string, so no dest check: trusted.
A non-string dest (number) is not checked: trusted.
dest written as the symlink-resolved path (on macOS the temp dir resolves through a symlink) while the input is the unresolved path: both resolve equal, trusted.
dest written as the unresolved temp path: resolves to the same directory, trusted.
dest is a symlink that resolves to the pack directory: trusted.
Receipt carrying only a revision: identity with null repo.
Receipt carrying only a repo: identity with null revision.
Empty-string repo_id and revision are not identity: no identity.
Empty repo_id is dropped, a non-empty revision kept.
A numeric repo_id is ignored; the string revision is kept.
Array repo_id and object revision are ignored: no identity.
A valid object receipt with neither repo_id nor revision: no identity.
A receipt that is a JSON array is not an object: no receipt.
A non-object receipt does not suppress the hub path identity.
JSON null is not an object: no receipt.
A bare JSON string is not an object: no receipt.
An empty receipt file is not JSON: no receipt.
Truncated JSON: no receipt.
A trailing comma is invalid JSON per the spec, but Foundation JSONSerialization accepts it. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: Python json rejects trailing commas; mirroring Foundation leniency would need a tolerant parser. Conservative direction (Python reads no receipt where the engine reads one).

cases.why: Invalid UTF-8 (0xFF) before the document: unreadable as JSON, no receipt, and no exception.
Invalid UTF-8 inside a string value of an otherwise valid document. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
UTF-8 BOM before valid JSON: Foundation skips the BOM. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
A bare NaN literal next to a valid repo_id (not strict JSON). Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
Duplicate repo_id keys: Foundation keeps the FIRST (Python json default keeps the last). Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
Valid object followed by trailing text. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
A JSON \u escape in repo_id decodes to the real character.
A raw TAB inside a JSON string (strict JSON forbids it). Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
A lone surrogate escape in an unrelated string value. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
An out-of-range number 1e999 beside a valid repo_id. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
A number with a leading zero (invalid JSON). Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
A bare Infinity literal beside a valid repo_id. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
600 nested arrays beside a valid repo_id. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
Single-quoted JSON. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
A // comment inside the document. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
Duplicate repo_id where the first is a number and the second a string. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
Three duplicate repo_id keys: the first wins in the engine. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
UTF-16LE with BOM is accepted by Foundation. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: Foundation auto-detects UTF-16/32 JSON; Python reads receipts as UTF-8 only. Conservative direction (Python reads no receipt where the engine reads one).

cases.why: UTF-16BE without BOM is accepted by Foundation. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: Foundation auto-detects UTF-16/32 JSON; Python reads receipts as UTF-8 only. Conservative direction (Python reads no receipt where the engine reads one).

cases.why: UTF-16LE without BOM is accepted by Foundation. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: Foundation auto-detects UTF-16/32 JSON; Python reads receipts as UTF-8 only. Conservative direction (Python reads no receipt where the engine reads one).

cases.why: UTF-32LE with BOM. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
A form feed as whitespace before the document. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
An invalid string escape \x. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
A NUL byte after the document. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
A 5000-digit integer beside a valid repo_id. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
5000 nested arrays: must read as no receipt without any exception. Expectation is engine-observed, not independent.
A literal backslash followed by the text ud800 is NOT a surrogate escape: valid. Hand-authored.
A valid surrogate pair escape is fine: valid. Hand-authored.
Hub snapshot directory: repo org/name, revision is the 40-hex snapshot name.
A trailing slash on the input path does not change the identity.
Uppercase hex is not a full lowercase 40-hex revision: revision null, repo kept.
39 hex characters: revision null, repo kept.
41 hex characters: revision null, repo kept.
A 64-hex (sha256-length) snapshot is not a commit revision: revision null, repo kept.
40 characters with a non-hex letter: revision null, repo kept.
A named snapshot (not a hash): revision null, repo kept.
models--a--b--c splits at the FIRST -- after models--: repo a/b--c.
models--single has no --: the whole segment is the repo.
models---a: encoded '-a' contains no --, whole segment is the repo.
models--a---b: first -- at index 1 -> org a, model '-b'.
models----name has an empty org half: component skipped, no other candidate -> no identity.
models--org-- has an empty model half: skipped -> no identity.
models-- with nothing after: skipped -> no identity.
An inner component with an empty half is skipped and the walk continues outward to an enclosing models--/snapshots pair (whose snapshot name 'outer' is not a hash).
Two models--/snapshots pairs: walking from the end, the innermost wins (repo and revision).
A pack directory below the snapshot: the enclosing snapshot still names repo and revision.
snapshots/<hex> under a directory not named models--*: no identity.
models--org--name/<hex> with no snapshots component: no identity.
Input 'snapshots/<hex>/..' resolves to the snapshots directory, which is not a snapshot: no identity.
A .. component is collapsed before the layout is read: snapshots/<hex>/../<hex> is the snapshot.
A .. path that leaves the hub tree for a plain directory carries no hub identity.
A symlink to a hub snapshot is resolved before the layout is read.
The hub dir itself is reached through a symlinked parent.
Receipt is a sibling of the symlink path the caller passes; dest names the real directory, which resolves equal: trusted.
Receipt sits beside the link TARGET, not beside the path passed in: the sibling of the passed path is what is read, so no receipt.
Same repo from both: the receipt revision wins over the path hash.
Receipt names the repo only: the missing revision is filled from the path.
Receipt names a revision only: the missing repo is filled from the path.
Same repo; the path snapshot is not a hash so it contributes no revision.
An empty receipt repo_id is not a repo, so it cannot conflict with the path.
Receipt and hub path name different repos: conflict.
Repo comparison is exact: org/Name vs org/name conflict.
A dest-less (trusted) receipt naming a different repo than the path conflicts.
Path repo 'single' vs receipt 'org/single': different, conflict.
